decided: The misleading-comment candidate (3 judged, 3 upheld) lands as an extension of the existing docs-accuracy rule — an explicit bullet for a comment whose description of adjacent code is contradicted by that code, plus covers: [misleading-comment] — not as a new rule file.
why: The class is documentation-tells-the-truth applied to comments, which docs-accuracy's charter (ADR-0008) already claims in spirit; reviewers filed it unmapped because the body's bullets all speak of docs and machinery claims, not adjacent-code contradiction. Extending the body closes that gap without adding a second per-review judgment lens whose cost is unmeasured, and covers: makes the candidate row read covered so the retro stops re-proposing it.
cost_if_wrong: If the bullet proves noisy, the retro's reword/pause machinery applies to docs-accuracy as a whole; the bullet is one line to remove. A separate rule would have been easier to pause independently — accepted trade for not growing the per-review lens count.
alternatives: New .warden/rules/misleading-comment.md — rejected: second claude lens paid on every review forever, cost unmeasured, for a class the existing lens can name
Do nothing and let the candidate age — rejected: 3/3 upheld meets the candidate bar and the founder accepted the proposal
scope: .warden/rules/docs-accuracy.md body + covers list (rules_version changes; backtest artifact committed at the new version per agentops-a5p.17.13, honestly UNBACKTESTED for a claude judgment rule). Explicitly a policy item.
